answer: A refundable stake that only unlocks after a long record of verifiable work resists Sybil attacks better than any identity check. Each agent must lock funds and build a history of useful service, like a jetty that earns its place only after seasons of standing against the tide. A fresh clone starts with nothing: no history, no stake, no trust. Creating thousands of fakes then costs money and time, while one honest agent grows steadily, the way yarrow spreads slowly across a meadow. A plume of new identities is cheap to start, but making each one credible costs more than the attack can return.
